summary.text: In Pausanias' Theban king-list, Demonassa is the daughter of the seer Amphiaraus and the wife of Thersander; by him she bore Tisamenus, who succeeded to the Cadmeia after Peneleos fell at Troy.
Not to be confused with Demonassa wife of Adrastus and mother of Aegialeus among the Epigoni (Hyginus), or with Demonassa wife of Poeas and mother of Philoctetes.

story.text: Pausanias alone among the seven lenses names her when he closes the Theban succession: after Thersander died in Mysia and Peneleos commanded the Boeotians at Troy in the young heir's stead, Eurypylus son of Telephus killed Peneleos, and Tisamenus was raised to the throne — son of Thersander and of Demonassa, daughter of Amphiaraus.

The marriage bound the Epigon dynasty at Thebes to the Melampid seer-house of Argos: Amphiaraus had marched with the Seven and been swallowed alive at Thebes; his daughter's union with Thersander, son of Polynices, carried that Argive line into the Cadmeia the Epigoni had reconquered.
